entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15156"/><div sID="gen29174" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15156"/><hi type="bold">18-23. the Jews did not believe ... he had been born blind ... till they called the parents of him that had received his sight--</hi>Foiled by the testimony of the young man himself, they hope to throw doubt on the fact by close questioning his parents, who, perceiving the snare laid for them, ingeniously escape it by testifying simply to the identity of their son, and his birth-blindness, leaving it to himself, as a competent witness, to speak as to the cure. They prevaricated, however, in saying they "knew not who had opened his eyes," for "they feared the Jews," who had come to an understanding (probably after what is recorded, <reference osisRef="John.7.50">Joh 7:50</reference>, &c.; but by this time well known), that whoever owned Him as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue--that is, not simply excluded, but excommunicated. <div eID="gen29174" type="x-p"/>

They prevaricated, however, in saying they "knew not who had opened his eyes," for "they feared the Jews," who had come to an understanding (probably after what is recorded, Joh 7:50 , &c.; but by this time well known), that whoever owned Him as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue--that is, not simply excluded, but excommunicated.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15167"/><div sID="gen29187" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15167"/><hi type="bold">39-41. Jesus said--</hi>perhaps at the same time, but after a crowd, including some of the skeptical and scornful rulers, had, on seeing Jesus talking with the healed youth, hastened to the spot.<div eID="gen29187" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29188" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that they which see not might see, &c.--</hi>rising to that sight of which the natural vision communicated to the youth was but the symbol. (See on <reference osisRef="John.9.5">Joh 9:5</reference>, and compare <reference osisRef="Luke.4.18">Lu 4:18</reference>).<div eID="gen29188" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29189" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that they which see might be made blind--</hi>judicially incapable of apprehending and receiving the truth, to which they have wilfully shut their eyes. <div eID="gen29189" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 39-41. Jesus said-- perhaps at the same time, but after a crowd, including some of the skeptical and scornful rulers, had, on seeing Jesus talking with the healed youth, hastened to the spot. that they which see not might see, &c.-- rising to that sight of which the natural vision communicated to the youth was but the symbol. (See on Joh 9:5 , and compare Lu 4:18 ). that they which see might be made blind-- judicially incapable of apprehending and receiving the truth, to which they have wilfully shut their eyes.
entries.reader_content_plain: 39-41. (See on Joh 9:5 , and compare Lu 4:18 ). that they which see might be made blind-- judicially incapable of apprehending and receiving the truth, to which they have wilfully shut their eyes.
